notes.meaning: Jesus walks away from the temple in Jerusalem for the last time. As He leaves, His disciples call His attention to the massive stones and beautiful buildings of the complex. They admire the grand structure, but Jesus sees that its time is drawing to a close.

Jesus tells the disciples that this magnificent temple will be totally destroyed. Not a single stone will remain sitting on top of another. His words came true forty years later when the Roman army burned the city and tore the temple down to its foundations.

Jesus sits on the slopes of the Mount of Olives looking across the valley at the temple. Four of His disciples approach Him quietly to ask when these events will take place. They want to know what sign will announce His coming and the end of the age.

Jesus starts His answer with an urgent warning against being misled. Troubling times always tempt people to believe clever lies. His followers must stay alert so that false teachers do not steer them away from the truth.

Many deceivers will appear and claim to be the Christ, which means the Messiah or God's promised deliverer. Because the people longed for rescue from Rome, many would follow these impostors. Believers must not be tricked by anyone who makes such claims.

Jesus warns that his followers will hear battles nearby and reports of conflicts far away. He tells them not to panic when they hear this news. These hardships must take place under God's plan, but they do not mean the final end has arrived yet.

Different nations and rulers will rise up and wage war against one another. In addition to human violence, food shortages and earthquakes will strike many regions. These disruptions show how unstable the world becomes before God brings His judgment.

Jesus compares all these early disasters to birth pains. Just as contractions signal that a birth is coming but are not the delivery itself, these troubles are only the beginning of sorrows. Believers should know that harder trials will follow before God renews all things.

Rulers and enemies will arrest, torture, and execute followers of Jesus. Christians will face universal hatred from people of all nations simply because they bear His name. Standing with Jesus requires being ready to suffer for His sake.

Under the pressure of persecution, many people who claimed to follow Jesus will abandon their faith. To save themselves, these former friends will turn against loyal believers and betray them to their enemies. Fear will turn professed love into bitter hatred.

Many false prophets will show up within and around the community of faith. These teachers will twist the truth and successfully trick large numbers of people. God's people must test every teaching against the message of Christ.

Lawlessness and evil deeds will spread rapidly through society. As wickedness becomes common, the warm love that believers have for God and each other will turn cold. Guarding a loving heart is essential when living among cruel and selfish people.

Only the person who remains faithful through all these trials to the end will receive salvation. True faith is proven by holding fast to Jesus despite danger, deceit, and suffering. God promises safety and eternal life to those who do not give up.

The good news about the kingdom of God will be proclaimed across the whole inhabited earth as a witness to all peoples. Only after this message is heard will the end come. God will not bring the final judgment until His offer of mercy has been announced far and wide.

differ.view: This prophecy points forward to a global preaching campaign that must reach every unreached ethnic group before Christ returns.
This was largely fulfilled before AD 70 as the apostles carried the gospel throughout the Roman Empire prior to the destruction of Jerusalem.

notes.meaning: Jesus tells His listeners to watch for a dreadful sacrilege standing in the holy place, which Daniel the prophet had foretold. An abomination of desolation refers to a filthy, idolatrous desecration that makes a holy site desolate. Readers are urged to pay close attention and understand what it signals.

When that terrible desecration appears, anyone living in Judea must immediately run for safety into the mountains. Trying to take shelter inside the fortified walls of Jerusalem will lead to destruction instead of safety. Believers followed this command by escaping across the Jordan River to the hills of Pella before the city fell.

differ.view: This flight applies directly to Jewish believers escaping the future Antichrist in the final days of history.

notes.meaning: A person who is relaxing or praying on a flat roof must not head downstairs into the house to rescue possessions. The outside stairs should be used to flee instantly. Saving one's life is far more urgent than saving material goods.

A farmer working out in the open fields must not go back to town to retrieve his outer cloak. Taking time to pack or grab extra clothing could cost a person their life. Escape must be swift and immediate.

Jesus expresses deep sympathy for pregnant women and mothers nursing infants during that terrible time. Having babies makes it agonizingly hard to run away quickly or endure the starvation of a siege. His words show heartfelt sorrow rather than an announcement of judgment on them.

Jesus instructs the disciples to pray that their escape will not happen in winter or on a Sabbath day. Cold rain, swollen rivers, and mud would make winter travel miserable and dangerous. Fleeing on the Sabbath would be difficult because city gates were closed and travel was strictly limited by Jewish customs.

The suffering during that period will be great tribulation, worse than anything experienced since the world was created. The horrors of famine, disease, and slaughter inside the besieged city were beyond human description. Jesus warns that this catastrophe will have no equal in history.

differ.view: This verse describes an unprecedented, worldwide period of tribulation that is still future and will take place just before Christ's return.
This referred primarily to the horrors of the siege and destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70, though it may also foreshadow end-time events.

notes.meaning: If God did not shorten the duration of that brutal siege, no human being in the region would survive. For the sake of the elect, which means His chosen people, God cut the days of terror short. Even in the midst of fierce wrath, God sets limits to protect His own.

During that crisis, people will shout that the Messiah has arrived in some special spot. Jesus commands His followers not to believe these excited rumors. Desperation makes crowds easy to mislead, so believers must stay grounded in what Christ has taught.

Impostors claiming to be the Messiah and counterfeit prophets will perform amazing wonders and signs to mislead the crowds. Their tricks will be so convincing that even God's chosen people would be fooled if that were possible. Miracles by themselves do not prove that a teacher comes from God.

Jesus reminds His disciples that He has warned them about these traps before they happen. Because they have been told in advance, they have no excuse for being swept away by false claims. Believers can stand firm because their Lord prepares them for every trial.

If deceivers claim the Messiah is out in the remote desert, believers must not go look. If others whisper that He is hiding in a private back room, they should not believe it. The true return of the King will not be a secret gathering or an isolated rumor.
